","type":"text/x-markdown"},"/home/runner/work/tw-plugin-library/tw-plugin-library/wiki/plugins/rimir/dashboard/README.md":{"title":"/home/runner/work/tw-plugin-library/tw-plugin-library/wiki/plugins/rimir/dashboard/README.md","text":"# tw-dashboard A TiddlyWiki 5 plugin (`$:/plugins/rimir/dashboard`) that turns any tiddler into a **free-form dashboard**: a canvas onto which you drop other tiddlers as freely arrangeable tiles. ## What it does - Tag a tiddler with `$:/tags/rimir/dashboard` and its body becomes a canvas. - **Add tiles** by dragging tiddlers onto the canvas from anywhere in the wiki, or by typing a title and pressing *Add tile*. - **Batch-add by filter** — type a filter in the box above the canvas and press *Add matching* to drop a tile for every tiddler it selects, arranged in a grid. - **Clean** — remove tiles in one go (with a confirmation). Leave the clean filter empty to clear the whole dashboard, or give a filter to remove only the tiles whose target it selects. - **Fit to screen** — a toolbar toggle that scales the whole board down so everything is visible at once, sized to fit your window — handy on a small display. Shrink-only, remembered per dashboard, and dragging/resizing stays accurate while fitted. - **Fullscreen** — a toolbar button that shows the dashboard fullscreen (the whole screen, without the wiki chrome); press again or Esc to exit. Combine with *Fit to screen* to see the entire board at once. - **Move** a tile by dragging its title bar; **resize** it from the bottom-right corner. Geometry is saved on release. - **Bring-to-front** — interacting with a tile raises it; the `z`-order persists. - **Two styles** per tile: a *window* tile with a title bar, or a *bare* tile that is just the resizable content. - **Corner controls** — a tile's controls appear in the corner on hover or keyboard focus. When the target has an external link an ↗ open-external button sits beside the ⋮ _actions_ menu, which opens on hover/focus with ⧉ show-in-popup, ⊟ toggle window/bare, × remove. - **Collapse a tile** — window tiles have a ▸/▾ toggle: a collapsed tile shrinks to just its headline, or — if its target has an `icon` — to just that icon (click to expand, drag to move, hover for the caption). - **Attach a file — drop or paste** — drop an image (or other media) onto a tile, or click the tile's 📋 corner button and press Ctrl+V to paste one from the clipboard. The file is uploaded to the filesystem location *derived from that tile's target* — a configured [rimir/file-upload](https://github.com/rimir-cc/tw-file-upload) scattered location when the target's namespace matches one (e.g. a `work/…` target files into the `work` location alongside that item), otherwise the default `files` location — and added as a new tile beside it. Dropping/pasting on a group (or its canvas) files into the group's *context* location and adds a child; the plain canvas uses `files`. Requires the file-upload plugin. - **Drop onto a collapsed tile** — a collapsed tile or group is still a drop/paste target: drop a tiddler or file onto a collapsed *group* to add it as a child (the group then expands), or drop/paste a file onto a collapsed *content tile* to file it in the tile's derived location. No extra chrome — the box is just outlined while you drag over it. - **Choose what a tile shows** — a tile transcludes its target's body by default; an uploaded image or PDF (with a `_thumbnail_uri`) shows its **thumbnail**, and a tiddler with no text but an `icon` shows the icon. Override per tile from the ⋮ menu (*Show*: auto / body / icon, or any field name), or set per-dashboard **display rules** (a target filter → the field to show) from the *Display rules* panel. - **Group (meta) tiles** — *Add group* creates a container tile that is itself a mini-canvas: drop tiddlers into it, drag existing tiles in and out, and nest groups inside groups recursively. Collapse to a header bar with ▸/▾, rename inline, and see the child count. Give a group an `icon` and it shows small before the name — or, when collapsed, becomes the whole header (hover for the name, click to expand). Removing a group promotes its contents to the parent container. - **Link a group to a tiddler (its context)** — connect a group to a tiddler as its _implicit context_: open the group's ⋮ menu → _Context…_ and name a tiddler (or drop a tiddler onto the group header). The group adopts that tiddler's caption (editable independently afterwards), shows its [`rimir/kind`](https://github.com/rimir-cc/tw-kind) icon in the header (click to open the tiddler in the story river), and — when the context is a kind instance — gains the same ✎ _entity_ popup a content tile has, so **Add child** creates instances with `parent` pre-set to the context _and drops their tiles inside this group_. _Unlink_ from the same menu (the caption is kept). - **Click to open** — a click (not a drag) opens the tile's target tiddler in the story river. - **Open a link in a new browser tab** — if a tile's target carries a `url` (or `_canonical_uri`) field, its **caption is rendered as a link** (hover to see the address in the browser status bar; click to open it in a new tab). The tile also shows an ↗ action, and **Ctrl/Cmd-clicking** the tile does the same (an uploaded image or file tile opens its raw file this way). Plain click elsewhere on the tile still opens the target in the wiki. The fields consulted and their priority are configurable. - **Open a tiddler in a new browser tab** — for a tile whose target has _no_ external link, the ⋮ menu offers an ↗ item that opens the target tiddler itself in a new tab, via its permalink. - **Ctrl-drag to duplicate** — hold Ctrl (or Cmd) as you start dragging a tile to drop a *copy* of it elsewhere (even into another group), leaving the original in place. The same tiddler can appear on as many tiles as you like. - **Ctrl-drag a group to reference it** — the same gesture on a *group* drops a live **reference**: a linked copy (brighter grey, with a 🔗 badge) that shows the same contents, name and icon. Work in any copy as if it were the original — renaming it, changing its icon or context, and adding, removing or re-arranging its children all reflect on the original and every reference at once. Each copy keeps its own position, size and collapsed state. Remove a reference and the original stays; remove the original and it asks first, telling you how many references go with it. A reference's ↗ control (revealed on hover, beside its ⋮ menu) **jumps to the original** — opening its parent groups, scrolling to it and flashing it red. - **Find a tile** — the *Find* box above the canvas locates a tile by caption: type text and each *Find* jumps to the next match — opening its parent groups, scrolling to it and flashing it red. - **Show contents in a popup** — the ⧉ control opens the target in a centered popup rendered through TiddlyWiki's default ViewTemplate (title, tags, fields and body), without leaving the dashboard. Close it with the × button or by clicking the backdrop. - **Kind-aware** — when a tile's target is a [`rimir/kind`](https://github.com/rimir-cc/tw-kind) instance, the window tile shows the type's icon (with the type name as hover text) before the caption. Degrades silently when kind isn't installed. - **Edit & extend kind entities** — for a tile whose target is a [`rimir/kind`](https://github.com/rimir-cc/tw-kind) instance, a ✎ *entity* control appears next to the ⋮ menu; hovering it opens a compact popup (the same actions as *Kind: Instances Overview*): **edit** opens the live editor modal, and **Add child** offers a button per kind whose `parent` accepts this entity's type — creating the child with `parent` pre-set (same validation/title-formula as the Creator) *and dropping a tile for it into the same group as the source tile*. Only shown when kind is installed and the target is an instance. ## Quick start 1. Click **New dashboard** in the page controls (right sidebar → Tools), or tag any tiddler `$:/tags/rimir/dashboard`. 2. Drag a few tiddlers onto the canvas. 3. Move, resize, and restyle them; click one to open it. ## Storage Each tile is its own system tiddler tagged `$:/tags/rimir/dashboard/tile`, stored under `$:/config/rimir/dashboard//tiles/…` with plain fields (`target`, `x`, `y`, `w`, `h`, `z`, `style`). No JSON blobs — every mutation is an ordinary `$action-setfield`. ## Requirements TiddlyWiki >= 5.4.0. No other plugin dependencies. Rich documentation renders when [`rimir/doc-template`](https://github.com/rimir-cc/tw-doc-template) is installed. ## License MIT — see [LICENSE.md](LICENSE.md). A group //reference// now shows a ↗ control on hover (beside its ⋮ menu, the same glyph as the open-external-link button) that jumps to the original group: it opens whatever parent groups are collapsed around the original, scrolls the board to it, and flashes it red briefly. A new ''Find'' box above the canvas does the same for any tile by ''caption'' — type text and press //Find// to reveal the first match (with a match count), press again to cycle through the rest. Matching is case-insensitive over each tile's effective caption (a group's name, a content tile's target caption/title, or a reference's original name) | |0.0.35 |2026-07-16 |Fixed: on a ''collapsed'' tile or group the hover 📋 paste button sat on top of the ▸ expand toggle and made it unclickable — you couldn't reopen the tile. The paste button is now shifted right of the toggle (it may overlap the caption instead, but only shows on hover), so the expand toggle stays clickable | |0.0.34 |2026-07-16 |Added group ''references'' — Ctrl/Cmd-drag a //group// (the same gesture that duplicates a content tile) to drop a live, linked copy of it anywhere on the dashboard. A reference (shown in a brighter grey with a 🔗 badge) mirrors the source group's ''contents, name and icon'', and you can work in it as if it were the original: renaming, changing the icon/context, or adding, removing and re-homing children in //any// copy reflects on the original and every reference at once. Each copy keeps its ''own'' position, size and collapse state (so one can be expanded and another collapsed). Ctrl-dragging a reference makes another reference to the same original. Removing a reference leaves the original alone; removing the original asks for confirmation — telling you how many references will also be removed — then moves the group's contents up to its parent. A reference dropped inside its own group shows a short "can't be shown here" note instead of recursing | |0.0.33 |2026-07-16 |Fixed: dragging a subgroup ''out of'' its parent group only worked toward the right and bottom — dragging it left or up made it stick at the parent's edge instead of following the pointer out. The live drag position was clamped to the parent's own coordinate space, so it could never go past the top-left corner. The box now follows the pointer freely in //every// direction while dragging (staying visible via the existing un-clipping), and the position is clamped back only when the tile stays in place — so a nested group can be pulled out to the root canvas or a sibling group in any direction | |0.0.32 |2026-07-16 |Fixed: on a board larger than the screen, starting to ''drag or resize'' a tile/group made the canvas ''jump to the top-left'' — the tile flew off to the side (over the wiki menu or off-screen) during the operation and snapped back on release. The drag styling flipped the scrolled canvas to `overflow: visible`, which forces its scroll position to 0. The body-cascade swap A dashboard is an ordinary tiddler tagged <>. The plugin ships a `ViewTemplateBodyFilter` step, `$:/config/ViewTemplateBodyFilters/rimir-dashboard`, ordered `list-before` the `default` step: ``` [tag[$:/tags/rimir/dashboard]then[$:/plugins/rimir/dashboard/body]] ``` So when a dashboard tiddler is viewed, its body renders `$:/plugins/rimir/dashboard/body` — the canvas — while its title, tags and fields render through the normal ViewTemplate. Nothing else about the tiddler is special. !! Tiles are tiddlers Each tile is its own tiddler tagged <>, stored under a system-tiddler prefix: ``` $:/config/rimir/dashboard//tiles/ ``` `` is the dashboard's `dashboard-id` field (auto-generated for dashboards made with the //New dashboard// button) or, as a fallback, the dashboard's title. Tiles carry plain fields — `dashboard`, `target`, `x`, `y`, `w`, `h`, `z`, `style` — so every operation is a plain `$action-createtiddler` / `$action-setfield` / `$action-deletetiddler`. There is no JSON serialisation to parse or rebuild, and the compact numeric fields keep the tiddlers in single-file `.tid` form. The canvas enumerates its tiles with: ``` [all[tiddlers]tag[$:/tags/rimir/dashboard/tile]field:dashboardnsort[z]] ``` Rendering in `z` order means DOM order and `z-index` agree. !! Groups and recursion A group (meta) tile is an ordinary tile with `role: group` and no `target`. Its body is a nested canvas. Membership is a single plain field: a tile's `dash-parent` holds the title of the group it lives in, and top-level tiles simply have no `dash-parent`. That makes the tiles of one dashboard a //tree//, and the canvas renders it with one recursive procedure: ``` dash-canvas(containerId) → lists tiles in that container → dash-tile dash-tile (role=group) → header + dash-canvas(thisGroupTitle) ← recurses ``` Each container is enumerated by the same shape of filter, differing only in the membership test — top-level uses `!has[dash-parent]`, a group uses `field:dash-parent`: ``` [all[tiddlers]tag[$:/tags/rimir/dashboard/tile]field:dashboard!has[dash-parent]nsort[z]] [all[tiddlers]tag[$:/tags/rimir/dashboard/tile]field:dashboardfield:dash-parentnsort[z]] ``` Because a child positions itself absolutely within its group's own `.rr-dash-canvas` (which is `position: relative`), the existing pixel-geometry model works unchanged at every level of nesting. Collapsing a group is just a `collapsed` field: when set, the body (and thus the whole subtree) is not rendered and the box is drawn at auto width //and// height, so it shrinks to its header; the stored `w`/`h` are preserved and reapplied on expand. Expanding also bumps the group's `z` to the front (guarded on the pre-toggle state) so its contents are not hidden behind sibling tiles. Removing a group re-homes its direct children to the group's own `dash-parent` — no recursive delete, no orphans. Because a collapsed tile renders no body, it would otherwise have no drop target. So when a tile is collapsed its header is wrapped as the drop surface: a `<$droppable>` (add-child) plus a nested `<$file-dropzone>` for a group, and a `<$file-dropzone>` for a content tile. Both wrappers are `display: contents`, so they contribute no box and the collapsed layout (shrink-to-header, controls positioning) is unchanged; the shared handle markup is factored into `dash-group-handle` / `dash-content-handle` so it is not duplicated between the wrapped and plain cases. The drop actions reuse the same `dashAddChildActions` / `dashTilePasteActions` strings as the canvas (a group drop appends `dashGroupExpand` to expand on drop). The only visual feedback is an `outline` drawn around the whole box via `.rr-dash-box:has(… .tc-dragover)` while a drag hovers — no permanent chrome. !! Group references A group can appear in more than one place at once as a ''reference'': Ctrl/Cmd-dragging a group (the same gesture that duplicates a content tile) drops a linked copy. A reference is an ordinary group tile carrying a `dash-ref` field pointing at the source group's title, and it ''delegates its whole identity'' to that source. Every group procedure resolves an effective `groupId` — `[get[dash-ref]] ~[]` — and reads the caption, icon, context, child list and child-count from `groupId` rather than from the tile itself. So the reference renders the //source's// canvas (`dash-parent = groupId`), and any edit made through a reference (rename, icon, context, add / remove / re-home a child) writes to the source and is reflected in the original and every other reference. Only the tile's own `x`/`y`/`w`/`h`/`z`, its container (`dash-parent`), and its `collapsed` state are per-copy — you can collapse or resize one reference without touching the others. Ctrl-dragging a reference makes a further reference to the same ultimate source (the new `dash-ref` is the dragged tile's `dash-ref` if it has one, else its own title), so references stay flat rather than chaining. Because a reference points at another group, it can create a cycle — a reference of //A// dropped inside //A// (or any descendant). To keep rendering finite, `dash-canvas` / `dash-tiles` thread a `chain` parameter: the space-separated list of `groupId`s already open in the current branch's ancestry. Before recursing into its body, a group tests `isCycle` = is my `groupId` already in `chain`; if so it renders a stub (`.rr-dash-ref-cycle`, "would place the group inside itself") instead of its canvas. Ordinary (non-reference) groups can never trigger this — `dash-parent` is a strict tree, so a group's id never appears twice in one ancestry. Deleting a reference removes only that tile; deleting the //original// while references exist opens a confirmation (it reports how many references will also be removed) and then deletes the references and promotes the source's children up to its container. !! Revealing a tile (go-to-original & Find) A reference's corner cluster carries a hover ↗ control (the same glyph as the open-external-link button) that jumps to the original group; the Find box in the toolbar does the same for any tile matched by caption. Both go through one primitive, `dash-reveal-actions(target)`: # `dash-expand-ancestors(target)` walks up the `dash-parent` chain and sets `collapsed=no` on each ancestor group that is collapsed (so the target will actually render), recursing to the root; # it writes the target's title into `$:/state/rimir/dashboard/reveal`. The `<$dashboard-drag>` widget takes a `reveal-state` attribute (that tiddler) and puts its tile title in a `data-dash-tile` attribute. On render and on a change to the reveal-state tiddler, the widget checks whether the requested title is its own; if so it defers a beat (so any just-expanded ancestors have laid out), calls `scrollIntoView` — which scrolls whatever scroll containers are available, in practice the root canvas — adds the `rr-dash-flash` class for a short red pulse, and clears the reveal-state (so the //same// tile can be revealed again — the next write is a fresh change). Scrolling and the one-shot flash are the parts that genuinely need JS; expansion, the button and the search are wikitext/CSS. Group bodies are `overflow:hidden` (not scrollers), so a tile positioned outside its parent group's box can't be scrolled to //within// the group — the common case (a top-level or in-box original) jumps correctly. The Find box computes matches with `dash.tile-cap` (a tile's effective caption — a reference resolves to its source's caption, a content tile to its target's caption/title) and a case-insensitive substring test, ordered by `z`. It reveals the match at a stored index and advances it, so repeated //Find// cycles through all matches and wraps. !! Attaching files: drop & clipboard paste Every content tile's body (and, for collapsed tiles/groups, its header; and each canvas) is wrapped in a `<$file-dropzone>` from [[rimir/file-upload|$:/plugins/rimir/file-upload]]. Where the uploaded file lands is //derived from the tile's target// (or a group's `dash-context`, or — for the plain canvas — its container group's context). Four single-line filter functions do the mapping, driven entirely by the configured locations tagged `$:/tags/rimir/file-upload/location`: ``` dash.fz-name(loctarget) first path segment of loctarget iff it names a configured location, else empty dash.fz-location(loctarget) that name, else the default "files" dash.fz-subfolder(loctarget) the rest of the path below that location (empty for files) dash.fz-title(loctarget,f) the media tiddler's title: "/" when scattered, else bare "" ``` So a tile targeting `work/mgm/foo` uploads into the `work` location under `mgm/foo/` (alongside that item), while a tile targeting a plain note falls back to `files`. This generalises the previous hard-coded `work/` handling to any location the user configures. A single `dashTilePasteActions` string (replacing the old `dashUploadActions` / `dashWorkUploadActions`) creates the media tiddler at the derived title, then a tile for it in the derived container (`<>` — a sibling for a content tile, a child for a group/canvas). The per-site `<$let>` sets `fzTarget` / `fzContainer` and the dropzone's `location` / `subfolder` attributes; the action resolves those variables at invoke time from the dropzone's scope. Clipboard paste needs no extra JS: the dropzone inherits TW-core's `paste` handler, which uploads a pasted image just like a dropped file. The only requirement is that the dropzone (or a descendant) hold focus when Ctrl+V is pressed. A shared `dash-paste-btn` procedure renders a small action-less `
